title: Structured Credit & CLOs - Analyst - New York
description:
**Job Description**  
  
As one of the world's top three credit ratings agencies, Fitch Ratings plays a critical role in global capital markets by providing supplementary credit analysis, ratings, research, and commentary to financial market participants. For over 100 years, Fitch Ratings has been creating value for global markets through its rigorous analysis and deep expertise, which have resulted in a variety of market leading tools, methodologies, indices, research, and analytical products. Fitch Ratings is part of Fitch Group, a global leader in financial information services with operations in more than 30 countries, which also includes Fitch Solutions. With dual headquarters in London and New York, Fitch Group is owned by Hearst.
  
  
At Fitch Ratings, credit analysts play a pivotal role in moving markets, as quality credit analysis is the lifeblood of our organization. With a legacy of over a century, our unique approach to credit ratings offers unmatched opportunities for professional growth. Embracing a "challenger mindset," you'll join a team dedicated to innovating service to our clients. Our people-driven analysis thrives on collaboration across all levels and locations, surpassing traditional financial modeling. Lastly, as part of our global community, you'll find inspiration, challenge, and support, with ample opportunities for visibility and influence in the global financial marketplace.
  
  
Want to learn more about a career as a credit analyst at Fitch Ratings? Visit: https://careers.fitch.group
  
  
**Fitch Ratings is seeking an Analyst to join its Structured Credit group to join our New York office** .
  
  
**About the Team:**

* Fitch Ratings is a global company with a presence in over 30 countries, offering opportunities to work with diverse teams and clients from around the world
* A collaborative, team-oriented work environment where excellent communication skills are essential
* An opportunity to be a lead coverage analyst at a global rating agency
* A role that aids debt capital markets in making more informed decisions through timely, insightful, and forward-looking rating actions and research

**How You'll Make an Impact:**

* Analyze new and existing ratings on Collateralized Loan Obligations (CLOs) using proprietary models
* Support transaction analysis, model review and drafting committee materials under guidance of senior team members
* Review transaction documents to identify and assess credit risks
* Prepare and present rating conclusions to a credit committee
* Draft rating action commentaries that explain rating decisions to market participants
* Contribute to recurring and ad hoc research publications

**You May be a Good Fit if:**

* You hold a bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, economics or a related quantitative field.
* At least one year of financial-sector experience, preferably but not necessarily related to Structured Credit or Structured Finance.
* You demonstrate strong analytical and problem-solving skills, intellectual curiosity, and attention to detail.
* You have excellent communication skills and can listen actively, incorporating different perspectives in a consensus-driven environment.
* You demonstrate personal responsibility, initiative, and self-management
* Ability to shift and quickly adapt between multiple tasks as priorities change
* You are proficient the Microsoft Excel and Word

**What Would Make You Stand Out:**

* Capital markets, securitization and/or credit analysis experience
* Proven track record of data-analysis of large datasets or working with programming tools, such as SQL, Python, VBA or comparable tools.

**Why Choose Fitch:**

* Hybrid Work Environment: 3 days a week in office required based on your line of business and location
* A Culture of Learning & Mobility: Dedicated trainings, leadership development, and mentorship programs designed to ensure that your time at Fitch will be a continuous learning opportunity
* Investing in Your Future

**Job Description**  
  
**Fitch Ratings is currently seeking Associate Analysts based out of our Chicago office.**  
  
Fitch Ratings is a leading provider of credit ratings, commentary, and research. Dedicated to providing value beyond the rating through independent and prospective credit opinions, Fitch Ratings offers global perspectives shaped by strong local market experience and credit market expertise. The additional context, perspective, and insights we provide help investors to make important credit judgments with confidence.
  
  
**What We Offer:**

* **The Fitch Ratings 2027 Associate Analyst Program (July 2027 cohort)** is an exceptional entry level opportunity for recent graduates. The full-time graduate program is a combination of structured training designed specifically to provide a broad analytical perspective and on-the-job learning experience. As an Associate Analyst, you'll be assigned to a specific Fitch Ratings product group and provided roles and responsibilities that fully immerse you in the credit rating process.
* During the 12-month program, Associate Analysts will get placed in analytical team where they will collaborate with senior analysts on new issuer ratings and gather and analyze the latest industry, regulatory, and economic information. At Fitch, you will receive the training to develop a high level of service to investors and issuers and a team-oriented approach to ratings analysis. Day to day work will include evaluating risk, participation in rating committees, drafting rating affirmations, and writing research reports.

**Application closing date: 29th January 2027**  
  
**We'll Count on You To:**

* Evaluate risk
* Participate in rating committees
* Draft ratings affirmations
* Write research reports

**What You Need to Have:**

* December 2026-June 2027 graduates; with less than 12 months of relevant full-time experience.
* Must be able to work in Chicago (hybrid office schedule)
* Ability to start July 2027
* Students must have work authorization in the U.S

**We're looking for:**

* Intellectually curious students with financial flair and a keen interest in credit, fixed income and industry analysis.
* Strong, clear, and concise communicators, both verbally and written
* Students from a diverse range of academic backgrounds with a passion for finance, research and analysis are welcome; A plus if you study one or more of the following majors: Real Estate, Finance, Economics, Accounting, and/or Political Science
* Individuals who truly value integrity and objectivity - these are two values we hold ourselves to and pride ourselves on

**Product groups and teams likely to be included are:**

* Structured Finance
* Corporate Ratings
* Financial Institutions
* US Public Finance
* Global Infrastructure and Project Finance Group

Read below to learn more about our different analytical groups.
  
  
**Structured Finance**  
  
Fitch's Structured Finance maintains existing ratings and assigns ratings to new structured finance transactions. Fitch currently rates Structured Finance transactions across four main asset classes: Asset Backed Securities, Residential Mortgage-Backed Securities, Commercial Mortgage-Backed Securities and Structured Credit.
  
  
**Corporate Ratings**  
  
The Fitch Ratings Corporates group provides public and private ratings on companies and their debt instruments, including - bank loans, senior and subordinated debt, commercial paper and preferred stock. The group's analytical methodology addresses the legal, regulatory and market environments in over 100 countries in which Fitch Ratings operates, with particular emphasis on debt structure.
  
  
**Financial Institutions**  
  
Fitch's financial institutions' coverage includes not only banks but also finance and leasing companies, securities firms, and asset management organizations. In addition, the group supports dedicated teams for rating specialized securities such as covered bonds.
  
  
**US Public Finance**

You'll work in a dynamic environment where innovation is encouraged, and collaboration is key to developing solutions that address the evolving needs of global markets. With a portfolio of best-in-class, award winning brands, we offer you the opportunity to advance your career while contributing to a company known for its expertise and commitment to excellence.
  
  
**Fitch Solutions is currently seeking a Financial Senior Analyst based out of our New York office.**  
  
**MAIN PURPOSE OF JOB:**  
  
The Finance Analyst will be responsible for collecting outstanding debts from global customers, allocating cash, resolving invoice queries, performing account reconciliations, and supporting debtor reporting within a busy, team-oriented global Accounts Receivable department.
  
  
**BACKGROUND TO THE DEPT:**  
  
The Accounts Receivable team is a global team and consists of 22 staff split between the New York and London offices. This position will be based in New York. This is a busy department, and it is important that the candidate can work well in a team environment.
  
  
**MANAGER'S VIEW OF THE ROLE:**  
  
This position is a key role in the Accounts Receivable team. The role involves collecting from global customers for payment of their invoices. This is a multi million-dollar ledger with a high volume of invoicing for large values. The right candidate will hit the ground running, will be keen to learn about the Business and build solid internal and external relationships. The successful candidate will need a clear and confident manner with both the Business and our customers. The candidate should have good Accounts Receivable experience with confidence to perform account reconciliations and assist with some monthly reporting where needed. The role requires a methodical individual with an eye for detail. With good organizational skills to ensure timely, well managed collections.  Akuna Capital is an innovative trading firm with a strong focus on collaboration,  cutting-edge technology, data driven solutions, and automation. We specialize in providing liquidity as an options market-maker – meaning we are committed to providing competitive quotes that we are willing to both buy and sell. To do this successfully, we design and implement our own low latency technologies, trading strategies and mathematical models.      

 Our Founding Partners first conceptualized Akuna in their hometown of Sydney. They opened the firm’s first office in 2011 in the heart of the derivatives industry and the options capital of the world – Chicago. Today, Akuna is proud to operate from additional offices in Sydney, Shanghai, London and Singapore.

 As a Trading Sneak Peek Program participant you will be enrolled in a crash course on the exciting world of options. You’ll learn from our dedicated trader trainers, as they introduce you to risk management, game theory, and optimal decision making. Outside the classroom, you’ll have the opportunity to apply your knowledge in real time.

**The Role**
------------

Mizuho is seeking a Senior Analyst or Associate to join Derivatives Risk Solutions Americas (DRSA), a team of salespeople and structurers that advises global corporations and financial sponsors on interest rate and foreign exchange risk. This seat sits within the team’s corporate coverage effort and is focused primarily on interest rate solutions: helping corporate treasury and finance teams manage the rate risk that comes with their balance sheets, their debt financings and their strategic transactions.

DRSA works where the bank’s lending, capital markets and M&A relationships meet the trading desk. A corporate client refinancing a term loan, pre-funding a bond issue, closing an acquisition or reshaping its fixed/floating mix needs a hedge that fits its financing, its accounting and its risk appetite. The team’s job is to spot those needs early, design the right solution, price it competitively with trading, and see it through execution and the life of the trade.

The team runs a lean, entrepreneurial model with a high bar. Junior team members are not confined to one lane: you will work directly with senior marketers on live pitches and transactions, build and price structures yourself, join client meetings, and over time take on coverage responsibility of your own. The role is client-facing and commercial. It suits someone who wants to grow into a derivatives marketer, not a pure modeler or risk analyst.

This version of the role is weighted toward corporate interest rate products, but we welcome candidates from across the derivatives solutions universe (sponsor and project finance hedging, corporate FX solutions, macro structuring) who want to build depth in corporate rates. * Track client financing activity (new issuance, refinancings, M&A, maturities) with coverage colleagues in corporate banking, debt capital markets and leveraged finance, so that hedging needs are identified before mandates are awarded.
* Prepare client-ready pitch materials, hedging analyses and recommendations; present them in client meetings and, as experience builds, lead technical discussions with treasury teams.

description:
**Group Overview**

The TP ICAP Group is a world leading provider of market infrastructure.

  

Our purpose is to provide clients with access to global financial and commodities markets, improving price discovery, liquidity, and distribution of data, through responsible and innovative solutions.

  

Through our people and technology, we connect clients to superior liquidity and data solutions.

Founded in London in 1866, the Group operates from more than 60 offices in 27 countries. We are 5,200 people strong. We work as one to achieve our vision of being the world’s most trusted, innovative, liquidity and data solutions specialist.

  
  

**Program Overview**

Our 10-week Global Broking Summer Internship offers a dynamic immersion into the world of institutional trading and operations. Interns gain hands-on exposure to the full trade lifecycle—from client onboarding to trade capture to settlement—while rotating across desks and asset classes within the world’s largest interdealer broker.

  

You’ll be part of a cohort of 10–15 Global Broking interns, joining a broader group of interns from across the organization. This structure fosters cross-functional learning and creates opportunities to build lasting professional relationships.

  

Program dates are Tuesday, June 1– Friday, August 6, 2027.

  

**Your Experience**

As a Global Broking intern, your summer will be shaped by real exposure to the business. You’ll spend your days embedded on active trading desks, learning directly from brokers and product specialists across a range of asset classes, including Fixed Income, FX & MM, Equities, Derivatives, and Emerging Markets.

  

Your day-to-day will include:

  

* Shadowing brokers during live trade execution; observing institutional price discovery in interdealer markets.

* Working on a summer-long capstone project in a small group, guided by a senior mentor, culminating in a final presentation to our C-Suite and other stakeholders.

* Practicing on student Bloomberg terminals to build fluency with market data and trading tools.

* Contributing to desk-specific mini-projects that reflect each product’s unique focus.

* Collaborating with peers on group initiatives and intern-led tasks.

* Exploring other functions across the firm—from operations and compliance to post-trade services.

* Participating in regular check-ins with the program coordinator for feedback and guidance.

* Learning & Development Workshops

* Volunteer and Community Engagement Events

Social and Networking Activities  

  

Each intern is matched with a dedicated one-on-one mentor to support their development throughout the program. These mentors offer career advice, help navigate the firm, and serve as sounding boards for questions and ideas.

  

Capstone groups are also paired with senior leaders who provide strategic guidance throughout the project.

  

**Eligibility Criteria**

To be considered, candidates must

* Be currently enrolled in an undergraduate program and pursuing a bachelor’s degree

* Have an anticipated graduation date of Spring 2028

* Be authorized to work in the United States (we do not offer visa sponsorship)

* Relocate at own cost if applicable; TP ICAP does not provide relocation or housing assistance
  

Ideal candidates are

* Curious and eager to learn, with a genuine interest in financial markets

* Adaptable and composed under pressure, with a willingness to take initiative

* Strong communicator

We specialize in providing liquidity as an options market maker – meaning we are committed to providing competitive quotes that we are willing to both buy and sell. To do this successfully, we design and implement our own low latency technologies, trading strategies, and mathematical models.   

 Our Founding Partners first conceptualized Akuna in their hometown of Sydney. They opened the firm’s first office in 2011 in the heart of the derivatives industry and the options capital of the world – Chicago. Today, Akuna is proud to operate from additional offices in Sydney, Shanghai, London and Singapore. 

 What you’ll do as an SOFR Floor Trader at Akuna:    

 We are seeking a Floor Trader to join Akuna’s trading team in the SOFR pit on the CME floor. The ideal candidate will be a highly motivated individual interested in supporting our team coverage and competing in the marketplace.    

 As a part of Akuna’s SOFR team, you will make markets in SOFR futures options in the CME pit and manage the resulting risk book. Whether being first to make a market or removing liquidity on a resting order, the opportunities you identify and execute on in the marketplace will be immediately represented in the team’s P&L. You will be entrenched in a collaborative and comprehensive team environment where you will have the opportunity to learn our systems and trading style from some of our most experienced traders. Your previous experience will be expected to provide value from day one even as you adapt to your new role. In this role you will:    

 Quote and trade SOFR options and multi-leg structures in the pit.

 2+ years trading rate options, market-making preferred

 Knowledge of the US rates front end and Fed policy

 Fast mental math, composure under pressure

 In addition to technical skillsets, Akuna values the unique perspectives people can bring to the table to collaboratively solve complex problems and drive Akuna forward. We want everyone to feel empowered to apply. We welcome your application and encourage you to take the first steps toward your future with us!   

 In accordance with Illinois Equal Pay Act, the minimum base salary starts at $145,000. Exact compensation offered may vary based on many factors including, but not limited to, the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and skill set. U.S. Bank Global Corporate Trust Services is one of the largest providers of corporate trust services in the world. Our clients look to us for trustee, agency, escrow, document custody and money market issuing services via our 48 domestic offices and three international offices.

The Collateralized Loan Obligation Group (CLO) is a division within Global Corporate Trust and Custody. CLOs are structured finance vehicles that issue both debt and equity liabilities, with the proceeds being used to buy a portfolio of collateral. Typical types of collateral include syndicated bank loans, corporate bonds, ABS, MBS, and Mezzanine debt. Investors can choose between a variety of risk return options.

The **CLO Deal Administrator 2** helps keep CLO portfolios running smoothly by handling the day‑to‑day operational work behind the scenes. location: New York, New York, United States
description:
About the position

 We're opening our first internships in the Formal Methods group of our OCaml Language team, which develops language features and tooling for correctness reasoning and bug finding in OCaml programs. With the emergence of agentic programming, we think formal methods will play a major role in helping validate agent-generated code and providing feedback for agents. Our vision is to make formal methods as useful a tool for building software as type systems are for us today, both by leveraging existing tools and technology, and pursuing novel approaches. 

 During the internship, we want to give you a real sense of what it's like to work at Jane Street full time while also providing a truly unparalleled educational experience. You'll be paired with full-time employees who act as mentors, collaborating with you on a real-world project that combines your research background with one of our active projects, such as adding support for property-based testing of formal specifications or developing a refinement type system for functional correctness verification. You’ll have the opportunity to evaluate the tools you develop on a large, actively developed production codebase. You'll also be able to attend guest speakers and social events, and hopefully get a real sense of what it would be like to work here full-time.

 There is plenty of work on combining agents and formal methods. What’s different at Jane Street is that we aren't stuck designing verification tools for legacy languages: we can modify and improve OxCaml, our branch of OCaml, and its development environment to make them well-suited for proof-driven software development. Moreover, we have a community of excellent programmers who are eager to adopt these tools and apply them to real software.

 Learn more about Jane Street's internship program here .

 About you

 We're looking for PhD students, postdocs, and masters students with outstanding research experience in program verification, programming language semantics, property-based testing, static analysis, model checking, and related areas. You should be

 A strong programmer who enjoys collaborating in small teams

 Excited to turn research ideas into practical tools

 Intellectually curious, humble and unafraid to ask questions 

 We don't expect you to have a background in finance, OCaml, or functional programming.

 If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

title: Sell Side Research Analyst
description:
**About Ornn**
--------------

Ornn is building the financial infrastructure for AI compute. Our price indices are live on Bloomberg Terminal. We structure and trade compute hedging instruments. And we're now building a platform that brings exchange-grade mechanics like order management, matching, scheduling, and settlement to how compute capacity gets reserved and allocated. We're a lean team in New York, backed by leading venture and strategic investors.

### **About the Role**

GPU compute is turning into an asset class, and almost nobody is writing about it with real data. You would be Ornn's first dedicated research analyst, publishing the work that hedge funds, consultancies, lenders and operators read to understand where compute prices are going and why.

You'll sit at the center of Ornn Data. Our index draws on more than 150 providers and roughly 1,000 transactions a day, and you'll turn that into research our clients pay for and our sales and markets teams use in every conversation.

### **What You'll Do**

* Publish regular research on the compute market: weekly pricing notes, monthly market reports, and deeper pieces on GPU generations, supply coming online, contract terms and residual values.
* Cover the companies that shape the market: hyperscalers, neoclouds, chipmakers, data center developers and their capex plans.
* Take calls with institutional clients, consultancies and lenders, and present at client meetings and industry events.
* Manage our freelance writers and researchers, set the research calendar and hold the bar on quality.

**Requirements**

* 1 to 4 years in equity or credit research, commodities research, or a research role at a fund, data provider or consultancy.
* Strong modeling skills in Excel and comfort working with large datasets.
* Clear, fast writing. You can turn a messy dataset into a sharp one-page view with a point of view.
* Real curiosity about AI infrastructure and how compute is bought, sold and financed.
* Comfortable working independently in a lean team.

**Nice-to-Haves**

* Sell side coverage of semiconductors, data centers, cloud or TMT.
* Experience with commodity markets, benchmarks or index products.
* Python or SQL.
* An existing following or published work in the AI infrastructure space.

### **Why This Role Matters**

A market only works when people trust the information about it. Ornn's index, futures work with ICE and data business all depend on being the most credible voice on what compute costs. This role is how that credibility shows up in the world every week, and how Ornn becomes the first place institutions go to understand the asset.

### **Compensation and Benefits**

Benefits include competitive salary, meaningful equity, health coverage, meals, and additional benefits.

### **Equal Opportunity Statement**

Ornn is committed to building a diverse team. We evaluate candidates based on their ability to do the work, not on pedigree or background. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences.

Compensation Range: $130K - $180K

description:
PIMCO is a global leader in active fixed income with deep expertise across public and private markets. We invest our clients’ capital across a range of fixed income and credit opportunities, leveraging our decades of experience navigating complex debt markets. Our flexible capital base and deep relationships with issuers have helped us become one of the world’s largest providers of traditional and nontraditional solutions for companies that need financing and investors who seek strong risk-adjusted returns.

Since 1971, our people have shaped our organization through a high-performance inclusive culture, in which we celebrate diverse thinking. We invest in our people and strive to imprint our CORE values of Collaboration, Openness, Responsibility and Excellence. We believe each of us is here to help others succeed and this has led to PIMCO being recognized as an innovator, industry thought leader and trusted advisor to our clients.

PIMCO is seeking an Analyst/Associate to join its Client Solutions & Analytics group in New York, NY or Newport Beach, CA. This group leverages PIMCO’s intellectual capital and resources to help our clients make better investment decisions. The group seeks to generate actionable investment insights for clients by combining a deep understanding of their objectives with an analysis of potential market opportunities and risks. The Analyst/Associate will participate in a development program designed for a career in investment management, providing broad exposure to financial markets, and portfolio analysis. The Analyst/Associate will assist Strategists in the group in running analysis on client portfolios, developing investment recommendations, and producing customized presentation materials.

* Four-year college degree with a major in Business/Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Engineering or applied science
* Minimum 3.2 cumulative collegiate grade point average, on a 4.0 scale or the equivalent, at an accredited 4-year college or university
* 0-4 years of experience in and enthusiasm for investment management
* Fluent in English (speaking, reading, writing)
* Must be willing to relocate to New York, NY or Newport Beach, CA, if not currently local

**Desired candidates should possess the following characteristics:**

* Interest in financial markets, macroeconomics, statistics, and investment modeling
* Strong analytical skill set and investment knowledge across asset classes, especially fixed income
* Demonstrated proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint; reasonable proficiency with Bloomberg, databases, and other analytic tools preferred
* Ability to relay complex ideas clearly
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills
* Desire to join a high performance, fast-paced culture
* Results-orientation, attention to detail and strong time management skills
* CFA designation or active status in program desired

**Responsibilities:**

* Support Strategists in analyzing client portfolios and building presentations that detail PIMCO’s analysis and conclusions
* Use proprietary software and external data sources to run risk analytics, optimizations, economic scenario analyses, and stress tests
* Manage a workload of multiple simultaneous projects while ensuring that deadlines are met
* Maintain standard presentation materials via periodic updates
* Develop an understanding of PIMCO investment strategies and their risks and benefits in different market environments
* Collaborate with Account Management, Analytics, and Product Strategy groups

To learn more, visit www.industriousoffice.com/careers.

**Pricing Analyst (Revenue Management)**
----------------------------------------

Industrious is the largest premium flexible workspace company in the world, operating over 250 locations across 10 countries as part of the CBRE portfolio. We design workplaces where teams feel welcomed, supported, and able to do their best work. The same principle guides how we work together as a company.

**About the Role**
------------------

Right now, the pricing judgment for Industrious's existing North America private office portfolio sits with one person who has built deep expertise in it: knowing which renewals need a bump, which office needs a promotion instead of a price cut, and which market is quietly slipping. That person is moving on to bigger things, and we need someone to step into that seat, formalize what works, and keep roughly 200 price changes a month running accurately, on time, and grounded in real conversations with the General Managers who run our buildings.

This is a Pricing Analyst, Revenue Management role, reporting into the pricing team. You will own business-as-usual pricing execution for the existing North America private office portfolio, with the scope to grow into other products and regions as the team expands.

**What Might Your Day Look Like**
---------------------------------

You start the morning scanning the pricing dashboard and notice a suite at 1411 Broadway that hasn't sold in weeks, while the identical suite next door is occupied at full list price. The GM has asked for a price cut. You pull the tour and application data, see it's a single-unit problem rather than a market problem, and decide a one-month promotion makes more sense than dropping the list price and setting up a harder renewal conversation down the road.

By mid-morning, you are on the phone with a GM in Nashville, walking through why an entire category of seven-to-nine person offices isn't moving. You ask about tour volume, application quality, and whether the floor plans still fit what people are searching for. You leave the call with a plan, and the GM leaves it feeling like someone actually looked at their building, not just their numbers.

In the afternoon, you work through the week's renewal batch, running each one against the pricing logic the team uses to decide what gets pushed through and what needs a second look. You flag one segment where occupancy has slipped two months running, log it for deeper review, and jot down a note on the decision tree so the next person doesn't have to relearn it from scratch.

You close the day updating the system with the changes you've made, checking your numbers against the portfolio report, and sending a short note to your manager on the one call that needs a decision above your pay grade.

title: Quant Risk Analyst - Derivatives & Clearing
description:
**About Polymarket**
--------------------

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform, where people trade on the outcomes of real-world events. As our markets, volumes, and derivative product suite grow, so does the sophistication of the risk infrastructure behind them. Our clearing and risk systems must operate with the rigor of a traditional clearinghouse while moving at the speed of a crypto-native trading platform.

**The Role**
------------

We're hiring a mid-level quantitative risk analyst to design and implement enterprise-scale risk models at the heart of our clearing operation. You'll own models for market risk, volatility and correlation of derivatives, stress testing, and automated liquidation — the systems that keep the platform solvent and users protected in fast-moving markets.

This is a hands-on role: you'll be building models in production code, not just specifying them. We expect you to work fluently with AI tools for development and research — and to be the skeptic in the room, pressure-testing AI-generated models and code against well-established risk frameworks before anything ships.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* Design, implement, and maintain enterprise-scale risk models covering market risk, margin, and counterparty exposure for a clearing organization.
* Build volatility and correlation models for derivatives, including calibration, backtesting, and ongoing model validation.
* Develop and run stress-testing frameworks: historical scenarios, hypothetical shocks, and reverse stress tests.
* Design and tune auto-liquidation logic — trigger thresholds, liquidation waterfalls, and safeguards against cascading liquidations.
* Use AI tools extensively to accelerate model development, coding, and research — and rigorously validate AI outputs against established risk models (VaR/ES, SPAN-style margining, GARCH-family volatility models, standard correlation frameworks) before deployment.
* Monitor model performance in production, investigate breaks, and iterate quickly.
* Partner with engineering, trading, and product teams to embed risk controls into platform architecture.
* Document model assumptions, limitations, and validation results to an audit-ready standard.

**What We're Looking For**
--------------------------

* 5–7 years of quantitative risk experience at a clearinghouse, exchange, prime broker, trading firm, or similar.
* Proven expertise designing and implementing risk models at enterprise scale — production systems, not just research prototypes.
* Deep experience modeling volatility, correlation, option skews, option pricing and implementing at scale for trad-fi derivatives, perpetuals, and fully collateralized event contracts.
* Hands-on experience with market risk modeling, stress testing, and auto-liquidation mechanics in a clearing context.
* Strong fluency with AI-assisted development and coding, paired with the judgment to pressure-test AI outputs against well-established risk models and catch what looks plausible but is wrong.
* Expert-level Python (numerical stack: NumPy, pandas, SciPy; solid software engineering practices).
* Advanced degree in a quantitative field (math, statistics, physics, financial engineering, CS) or equivalent experience.
* Strong mathematical foundation in stochastic calculus and linear algebra.

**Nice to Have**
----------------

* C# and/or C++ for performance-critical or production systems.
* Familiarity with crypto market structure, perpetuals, or prediction markets.
* Experience with CCP risk frameworks (CPMI-IOSCO PFMI, default management, margin methodology).
* Experience building real-time risk systems.

**Pay Transparency**
--------------------

Base salary range: $400,000 to $450,000, plus equity and benefits.

This is a good-faith range for the level we're hiring at. Experience varies widely within a title here, so if your expectations fall outside it, reach out anyway. We're always happy to talk it through.

Our employees are our greatest asset. We have spent years building a team of talented, dedicated technologists, data-driven traders, and expert leaders with an emphasis on our core pillars:People, Process, Trading Edge, and Technology. Simplex is an in-office organization, helping to foster a collaborative and communicative culture.

**Career Description**

We’re hiring an Algorithmic Trader focused on CME equity index futures. You’ll build and run short-horizon strategies at microsecond-to-second timescales: turning full-depth order book data into predictive signals, designing passive market-making logic for ES, and working with our C++ and FPGA developers to get your ideas into production. This role suits someone who has traded or researched ES/NQ in a low-latency environment and enjoys taking an idea from raw market data to live trading.

**What you will be doing**

* Research and build short-horizon (microsecond to second) price-prediction signals for CME equity index futures from full-depth order book and trade data: order aggressiveness, queue position, cancels, icebergs, and leads from related futures and cash equities.
* Own the signal pipeline end to end: packet-capture data, feature design, sampling, model fitting (linear and tree-based), pruning, out-of-sample simulation, and deployment with C++ and FPGA developers.
* Design and tune a passive ES market-making strategy: level joining, queue-priority value, order spacing, cancel/replace timing, exchange messaging limits, and protective pulls when latency or connectivity degrades.
* Model the matching engine: turn fill latency and book state into estimates of how many levels traded and future price changes, then use this information to move quotes, purge, and take liquidity in futures, index options, and equities.
* Measure and improve latency: profile order paths in microseconds, reconcile wireless and fiber timestamps across data centers, compare vendor signal feeds, and quantify misses against exchange reports.
* Write specs for developers, verify their output against your own calculations, and find bugs in production data and pricing pipelines.

Skills and experience

* 2+ years trading or researching CME equity index futures (ES/NQ) at a proprietary trading firm with sub-millisecond systems.
* Hands-on experience with CME MDP 3.0 order-by-order market data: book building, queue-position tracking, iceberg and self-match-prevention inference, matching-engine latency behavior.
* Built microprice or alpha models that ran live at microsecond horizons. Fluent in lead/lag analysis, half-lives, markouts, and adverse selection.
* Passive quoting experience on FIFO futures markets: queue value, join and cancel logic, messaging-efficiency constraints, mass-quote protections.
* Python research stack (polars or pandas, numpy, gradient-boosted trees, SQL). Reads C++. Has worked alongside FPGA or low-latency engineers.
* Bonus: index basis and roll (cash, futures, BTIC), SPX options, or microwave network latency.

 On our proprietary research team—Market Intelligence— you will uncover insights about markets and the broader economy through deep compliant fundamental research and applying data science and engineering techniques to alternative data sets. In partnership with our investment professionals and Compliance team, our team of analysts, data scientists and engineers work together to produce compliant research and build tools that inform our firm’s investments. We look for other bright, motivated, and collaborative people to join our team and grow with us—a majority of the leaders in our group were promoted from within.

 WHAT YOU’LL DO 

 As a Macro Analyst, Market Intelligence covering the US, you will work with alternative data to gather macroeconomic context and identify insights relevant to rates and FX markets. You will then partner with our team of data scientists and engineers to develop analyses that you deliver as synthesized insights to our investment professionals to help aid in their research processes. The work is ever evolving, affording opportunities to tackle new challenges alongside research teammates from diverse backgrounds. Specifically, you will:

 Analyze and interpret alternative data from multiple sources and develop subject-matter expertise on the key themes and KPIs that drive the markets within your assigned coverage

 Produce research for internal consumption by our investment professionals across a variety of channels, including written reports, verbal communication, data feeds, and visualizations

 Interact directly with our investment professionals to learn the macro investment process from them and help drive more informed investment decisions

 Collaborate with our proprietary research teams including Data Sourcing, Data Science, and Data Engineering, as well as Compliance, to source, evaluate, and draw value from new and existing data assets to produce actionable research for investment professionals

 An undergraduate degree or advanced degree with demonstrated academic success

 Proficiency with technical coding/programming and ability to participate in a live technical screen (SQL, Python)

 Experience with modelling and analyzing time series data as part of the macroeconomic or fundamental research process for business, public policy, finance, engineering, applied sciences, or other quantitative fields

 A passion for finance, research, and using data to solve problems

 Comfort with analyzing novel data and explaining concepts to non-technical partners

 Great organizational skills to handle a demanding workload, creativity, and a strong work ethic

 Ability to operate productively in a team environment

 Strong verbal and written communication skills

 Commitment to the highest ethical standards

title: Dean of Students, Academy of Math and Programming (AMP)
location: New York, New York, United States
description:
About the Position

 We are looking for an experienced school leader to serve as Dean of Students for our Academy of Math and Programming (AMP) in New York City.

 AMP is a residential program for recent high school graduates of diverse backgrounds who have experienced barriers to access and opportunity within advanced STEM education. 

 Students spend five weeks studying mathematics, computer programming, data analysis, and game theory while building a close academic and residential community.

 As Dean of Students, you will support the program's academic culture and help students meet our clear expectations for attendance, participation, classroom behavior, and academic integrity. To do this successfully, you’ll have to partner closely with instructors and teaching assistants, the program director, guidance counselors, and residential director to make sure students receive consistent support.

 Before the on-site program begins, you will partner with Jane Street’s AMP leads on program preparation, including helping develop the code of conduct. During the program, you will be on site from 9am to 5pm, Monday through Friday, while classes are in session. 

 Additional responsibilities will include:

 Consistently applying the program's code of conduct during the academic day and helping students address concerns related to attendance, engagement, academic integrity, and classroom behavior in a constructive and developmentally appropriate way

 Meeting regularly with instructors and teaching assistants to understand classroom dynamics and identify students who may need additional support

 Visiting classes periodically to observe student participation and the learning environment

 Meeting regularly with Jane Street’s AMP leads to align on program values and student expectations, discuss student concerns, and agree on key decisions

 This is a temporary, full-time summer position. The 2027 program will run from the end of June through the beginning of August. Jane Street deeply values the quality of our educational programming, and we compensate our high-caliber staff accordingly. Travel, housing (if requested), and meals will be provided.

 About You

 Have leadership or school administration experience in a middle or high school, summer program, or similar educational setting

 Experienced with supporting student conduct and academic expectations with sound judgment, empathy, and consistency

 A clear, collaborative communicator; comfortable giving direct feedback to students and staff

 Have strong observational and organizational skills, including the ability to notice patterns and follow up promptly

 Able to handle sensitive student matters discreetly and escalate concerns appropriately

 If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com .

title: Teaching Assistant, Academy of Math and Programming (AMP)
location: New York, New York, United States
description:
About the Position

 We are looking for enthusiastic Teaching Assistants with strong backgrounds in mathematics, computer science, or a related quantitative field for our Academy of Math and Programming (AMP) in New York City.

 This is a temporary, six-week summer role, including one week of training before the five-week student program. AMP is a residential program serving recent high school graduates of diverse backgrounds who have experienced barriers to access and opportunity within advanced STEM education.

 Students study mathematics, computer programming, data analysis, and game theory through challenging and interactive classes, problem-solving sessions, and games. You will work alongside instructors and other teaching assistants to support students in the classroom and help supervise the residential program.

 Teaching Assistants support both the mathematics and computer science curricula. We do not expect everyone to have equal depth across every topic. It’s fine if you have greater experience in one subject, as long as you are excited to support both subjects and learn alongside the instructional team.

 Additional responsibilities will include:

 Helping instructors deliver lessons in areas such as combinatorics, number theory, algorithms, programming, and software development

 Working with students individually and in small groups during classes, problem-solving sessions, and study hours

 Supporting classroom supervision, assignment review, and other academic coordination

 Teaching, guiding, and playing strategy games with students

 Residing with students in the dormitory for the duration of the program and serving as an active, responsible program leader beyond the classroom, supporting student well-being and reinforcing community expectations 

 Leading academic and social activities during evenings and select weekends

 Jane Street deeply values the quality of our educational programming, and we compensate our high-caliber staff accordingly. Travel, housing, and on-site meals will be provided.

 About You

 An undergraduate student in mathematics, computer science, or a related field

 Experienced with, or interested in, working with students in an academic or residential setting

 Have a strong background in mathematics, computer science, or both; it is fine to have greater depth in one subject than the other

 Comfortable with foundational programming and mathematical problem-solving, and willing to learn beyond your primary area of expertise

 A patient and encouraging communicator who enjoys helping students work through challenging material

 Exercises sound judgment, maintains clear boundaries, and handles sensitive student matters discreetly, escalating concerns when appropriate

 Having a genuine interest in strategy, logic, and mathematical games is preferred

 Available to live on site for the full program and support evening and select weekend activities

title: Floor Trader
description:
Our formula for success is to hire exceptional people, encourage their ideas and reward their results.

 As a Floor Trader , you will participate in a comprehensive training program designed to build your understanding of our products, markets, and approach to trading. You will split your time between the Cboe trading floor and DRW’s trading desk, gaining exposure to both floor-based and voice trading while developing the skills needed to take on increasing responsibility. You will work closely with experienced traders and brokers to understand market dynamics, evaluate trading activity, and improve the tools used to support real-time analysis and decision-making.

 How you will make an impact… 

 Contribute directly as a Floor Trader at DRW, building market knowledge and trading judgment through hands-on experience

 Analyze order flow, trading activity, and broker behavior to identify patterns and potential trading opportunities

 Develop, maintain, and enhance tools, models, algorithms, and systems that support trading analysis, visualization, and risk management

 Partner with traders and engineering teams to define requirements and help develop market-beating trading tools

 Monitor market activity and communicate timely, relevant market information to other team members

 Research new market opportunities and contribute ideas to the team

 Take on increasing ownership of trading decisions and risk as your knowledge and experience grow

 What you bring to the team… 

 A bachelor’s in economics, finance, mathematics, statistics, computer science or any related field and have an expected graduation date between December 2026 and June 2027 

 A genuine interest in financial markets and a desire to build a career in trading

 The ability to make thoughtful decisions in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment

 Strong communication skills and the confidence to interact effectively with traders, brokers, and other market participants

 A collaborative mindset, intellectual curiosity, and willingness to learn from feedback

 Prior trading or financial-markets experience is helpful but not required

 Proficiency in python is a plus

 DRW is a diversified trading firm with over 3 decades of experience bringing sophisticated technology and exceptional people together to operate in markets around the world.  We value autonomy and the ability to quickly pivot to capture opportunities, so we operate using our own capital and trading at our own risk. 

 Headquartered in Chicago with offices throughout the U.S., Canada, Europe, and Asia, we trade a variety of asset classes including Fixed Income, ETFs, Equities, FX, Commodities and Energy across all major global markets. We have also leveraged our expertise and technology to expand into three non-traditional strategies: real estate, venture capital and cryptoassets.

The ideal candidate displays strong mental math and excellent communications skills and is interested in being a part of a fast-paced and collaborative team environment. 

 After training, candidates will start with one of the following teams: 

 Options Market Making (and all the various desks) 

 Delta One 

 Vol Arb 

 Crypto 

 Quantitative Strategy Group 

 Qualities that make great candidates: 

 BS/MS/PhD degree in Engineering, Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Actuarial Science or a related/equivalent field must be completed upon employment 

 Strong math aptitude, numerical and quantitative analysis skills 

 The ability to communicate effectively and efficiently while fostering external professional relationships

 Entrepreneurial self-starter ready to work in a fast paced and competitive team environment 

 Desire to learn about financial markets and economic theories 

 Programming experience preferred 

 Major GPA of 3.5 or above

location: New York, New York, United States
description:
About the Position

 Our goals are to give you a real sense of what it's like to work as a Quantitative Trader at Jane Street while also providing a truly unparalleled educational experience. You'll be paired with experienced quantitative traders who will teach you how to identify market signals, analyze and execute strategies, construct quantitative models, conduct statistical analysis, and build trading intuition.

 At Jane Street, the lines between research, technology, and trading are intentionally blurry, and you’ll have access to petabytes of data, a computing cluster with hundreds of thousands of cores, and a growing GPU cluster containing tens of thousands of high-end GPUs. We don't believe in "one-size-fits-all" modeling solutions; we are open to and excited about applying all different types of statistical and ML techniques, from linear models to deep learning, depending on what best fits a given problem. You'll work closely with two different mentors on projects relating to their day-to-day work, giving you a sense of the variety of problems we solve every day. Past projects have included analyzing new or existing datasets, training predictive models, simulating potential new trading strategies, writing tools that we use in production, and even working to answer big-picture questions we haven't yet figured out.

 During the internship, your work is reinforced with intensive classes, workshops, and team-based mock trading sessions. These will expose you to many of the dynamics we observe in real markets, illustrate the role that we play in making markets more efficient, and help build intuition for how we think about both trading and collaborating.

 As a quantitative trading intern, you'll also have the opportunity to participate in one "elective" based on your interests. Electives consist of targeted classes and immersive activities, and are designed to give you a deeper and more nuanced look into one of the many aspects of what quantitative trading can look like at Jane Street:

 Machine Learning, Modeling, and Data Science 

 You'll learn how Jane Street applies advanced machine learning and statistical techniques to make models and predictions using large datasets of both real and simulated market data. You'll learn how to train and use a variety of ML models, and gain an understanding of the differences between textbook machine learning and its application to noisy and complex financial data. 

 Algorithmic Trading and Market Microstructure 

 You'll learn the end-to-end process of developing an algorithmic trading strategy. You'll analyze market data to develop a tradable fair value and implement a trading strategy in Python. Your algorithmic strategy will connect directly to simulated markets with different market structures, and you will learn how to optimize your strategy given the unique attributes of each market. You will discover how various market dynamics affect strategy behavior and learn how real-world trading differs from simulation.

 Trading Strategy and Scenarios 

 You’ll be introduced to a rotating set of new trading scenarios inspired by real events on a particular trading desk. You’ll work in teams on multiple mock trading sessions related to each scenario and use the time between sessions to refine your strategies, write recaps, and hear how the story played out in real life from our seasoned full-time traders who lived through it.

 About You

 If you’ve never thought about a career in finance, you’re in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind, a collaborative spirit, and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you’ll fit right in. We’re more interested in how you think and learn than what you currently know. You should be:

 A strong quantitative thinker (no specific degree or major is required)

 A clear and effective verbal and written communicator

 Someone who enjoys working collaboratively on a team

title: Tools and Compilers Research and Development
location: New York, New York, United States
description:
About the position

 We are excited to announce research internships in our Tools and Compilers group. We're looking for PhD and masters students with outstanding research experience in programming languages, compilers, verification, and related areas.

 Jane Street's Compilers team focuses on improving OCaml as a foundation for Jane Street's ever-growing technology stack, in collaboration with the greater OCaml community. We work on many different aspects of the compiler, aiming to make it easier for developers to express their ideas in OCaml, to improve the performance of the generated code, and to make the OCaml compiler itself faster and easier to use.

 Over the years, we extended the type system with support for novel language features, re-engineered the optimizer ground-up, and added feedback-directed optimization. We also extend and enhance the surrounding toolchain, working on tools for profiling, debugging, documenting, and building automation. The vast majority of our work is open-source, and we upstream as much as we can to the mainstream OCaml compiler.

 During the internship, you will work in collaboration with your mentors on one project for about 10-12 weeks. You'll learn how we use OCaml in our day-to-day work, and gain exposure to the libraries and tools that are foundational to our internal systems. You'll gain a better understanding of the wide range of problems we solve every day. You'll try out new ideas and apply state-of-the-art research to a large actively-developed production codebase.

 We'll pick a project that combines your research background with our active work on the OCaml compiler and core libraries. Example project areas include:

 Type systems that track locality and uniqueness

 Formal verification of OCaml programs

 New language features for systems programming

 Compiler testing and validation

 You'll also be able to access our physical and virtual educational resources, attend guest speakers and social events, and hopefully get a real sense of what it would be like to work here full-time.

 About you

 We're looking for PhD and masters students with outstanding research experience in programming languages, compilers, verification, and related areas. We don't expect you to have a background in finance, OCaml, or functional programming. Please include the list of your peer-reviewed publications in your resume.
